title: Google Code Jam
statementMd:
Many of you must be familiar with the Google Code Jam round rules. Let us remind you of some key moments that are crucial to solving this problem. During the round, the participants are suggested to solve several problems, each divided into two subproblems: an easy one with small limits (Small input), and a hard one with large limits (Large input). You can submit a solution for Large input only after you've solved the Small input for this problem. There are no other restrictions on the order of solving inputs. In particular, the participant can first solve the Small input, then switch to another problem, and then return to the Large input. Solving each input gives the participant some number of points (usually different for each problem). This takes into account only complete solutions that work correctly on all tests of the input. The participant gets the test result of a Small input right after he submits it, but the test result of a Large input are out only after the round's over. In the final results table the participants are sorted by non-increasing of received points. If the points are equal, the participants are sorted by ascending of time penalty. By the Google Code Jam rules the time penalty is the **time when the last correct solution was submitted**.

Vasya decided to check out a new tactics on another round. As soon as the round begins, the boy quickly read all the problems and accurately evaluated the time it takes to solve them. Specifically, for each one of the $*n*$ problems Vasya knows five values:

- Solving the Small input of the $*i*$-th problem gives to the participant $*scoreSmall*_{*i*}$ points, and solving the Large input gives $*scoreLarge*_{*i*}$ more points. That is, the maximum number of points you can get for the $*i*$-th problem equals $*scoreSmall*_{*i*} + *scoreLarge*_{*i*}$.
- Writing the solution for the Small input of the $*i*$-th problem takes exactly $*timeSmall*_{*i*}$ minutes for Vasya. Improving this code and turning it into the solution of the Large input takes another $*timeLarge*_{*i*}$ minutes.
- Vasya's had much practice, so he solves all Small inputs from the first attempt. But it's not so easy with the Large input: there is the $*probFail*_{*i*}$ probability that the solution to the Large input will turn out to be wrong at the end of the round. Please keep in mind that these solutions do not affect the participants' points and the time penalty.

A round lasts for $*t*$ minutes. The time for reading problems and submitting solutions can be considered to equal zero. Vasya is allowed to submit a solution exactly at the moment when the round ends.

Vasya wants to choose a set of inputs and the order of their solution so as to make the expectation of the total received points maximum possible. If there are multiple ways to do this, he needs to minimize the expectation of the time penalty. Help Vasya to cope with this problem.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*t*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ *t* ≤ 1560$). Then follow $*n*$ lines, each containing 5 numbers: $*scoreSmall*_{*i*}, *scoreLarge*_{*i*}, *timeSmall*_{*i*}, *timeLarge*_{*i*}, *probFail*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *scoreSmall*_{*i*}, *scoreLarge*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}, 1 ≤ *timeSmall*_{*i*}, *timeLarge*_{*i*} ≤ 1560, 0 ≤ *probFail*_{*i*} ≤ 1$).

$*probFail*_{*i*}$ are real numbers, given with at most 6 digits after the decimal point. All other numbers in the input are integers.

## Output

Print two real numbers — the maximum expectation of the total points and the corresponding minimum possible time penalty expectation. The answer will be considered correct if the absolute or relative error doesn't exceed $10^{ - 9}$.

## Note

In the first sample one of the optimal orders of solving problems is:

1. The Small input of the third problem.
2. The Small input of the first problem.
3. The Large input of the third problem.
4. The Large input of the first problem.

Note that if you solve the Small input of the second problem instead of two inputs of the third one, then total score expectation will be the same but the time penalty expectation will be worse ($38$).
statementZhMd:
许多人应该都熟悉 Google Code Jam 的比赛规则。让我们回顾一些对解决本题至关重要的关键内容。比赛期间，参赛者需要解决若干道题目，每道题目又分为两个子问题：限制较小的简单版本（Small input）和限制较大的困难版本（Large input）。只有解决了某道题目的 Small input 后，才能提交该题目的 Large input。除此之外，解决各个输入版本的顺序没有其他限制。特别地，参赛者可以先解决某题的 Small input，然后切换到另一道题，之后再回来解决前一道题的 Large input。解决每个输入版本都会获得一定数量的分数（通常每道题的分值不同）。只有在该输入版本的所有测试点上都正确的完整解答才能获得相应分数。参赛者提交 Small input 后会立即得到测试结果，而 Large input 的测试结果要等比赛结束后才能公布。在最终排名中，参赛者首先按所得分数非递增排序；如果分数相同，则按时间罚分递增排序。按照 Google Code Jam 的规则，时间罚分是**提交最后一个正确解答的时间**。

Vasya 决定在另一场比赛中尝试一种新的策略。比赛一开始，这个男孩就迅速读完了所有题目，并准确估计了解决它们所需的时间。具体来说，对于 $*n*$ 道题目中的每一道，Vasya 知道以下五个值：

- 解决第 $*i*$ 道题的 Small input 可获得 $*scoreSmall*_{*i*}$ 分，解决 Large input 还可额外获得 $*scoreLarge*_{*i*}$ 分。也就是说，第 $*i*$ 道题最多可以获得 $*scoreSmall*_{*i*} + *scoreLarge*_{*i*}$ 分。
- 编写第 $*i*$ 道题 Small input 的解答恰好需要 Vasya $*timeSmall*_{*i*}$ 分钟。改进这份代码并将其变为 Large input 的解答还需要 $*timeLarge*_{*i*}$ 分钟。
- Vasya 经常练习，因此所有 Small input 他都能一次通过。但 Large input 就没有那么容易了：有 $*probFail*_{*i*}$ 的概率，第 $*i*$ 道题 Large input 的解答最终会被判定为错误。请注意，这些解答不会影响参赛者的分数和时间罚分。

比赛持续 $*t*$ 分钟。阅读题目和提交解答所需的时间可以视为零。Vasya 可以恰好在比赛结束的时刻提交解答。

Vasya 希望选择一些输入版本，并确定解决它们的顺序，使最终获得总分的期望值最大。如果有多种方案都能达到最大期望分数，他还需要使时间罚分的期望值最小。请帮助 Vasya 解决这个问题。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*t*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ *t* ≤ 1560$）。接下来有 $*n*$ 行，每行包含 5 个数：$*scoreSmall*_{*i*}, *scoreLarge*_{*i*}, *timeSmall*_{*i*}, *timeLarge*_{*i*}, *probFail*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *scoreSmall*_{*i*}, *scoreLarge*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}, 1 ≤ *timeSmall*_{*i*}, *timeLarge*_{*i*} ≤ 1560, 0 ≤ *probFail*_{*i*} ≤ 1$）。

$*probFail*_{*i*}$ 为实数，小数点后最多有 6 位。输入中的其他数均为整数。

## 输出格式

输出两个实数：总分的最大期望值，以及在此条件下可能达到的最小时间罚分期望值。如果答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 $10^{ - 9}$，则视为正确。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，一种最优的解决顺序如下：

1. 第三道题的 Small input。
2. 第一道题的 Small input。
3. 第三道题的 Large input。
4. 第一道题的 Large input。

注意，如果解决第二道题的 Small input，而不是第三道题的两个输入版本，那么总分期望值仍然相同，但时间罚分期望值会更差（$38$）。
